Adams' Apportionment Method

ArithmeticCountingLogic

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Share a fixed number of seats between states so that each state's share matches its population.
How to play: Change the populations, seats or divisor. Press "Find divisor" to make the rounded-up shares add up exactly.
Number of seats 23 States 3
Look for the math

Dividing 23 seats among three states seems easy until the shares are not whole numbers. Different rounding rules give different parliaments, and one of them was proposed by a future president.

Quotas, up and down

The standard divisor is the total population divided by the number of seats. A state's standard quota is its population divided by that divisor, and the standard quotas always add up to the seat count exactly. Hamilton's method rounds those quotas and then adjusts. John Quincy Adams proposed instead to round every quota up, using a slightly larger divisor so the rounded totals still fit — a divisor method. The table shows the lower quota (rounded down at the standard divisor) beside the modified and upward ones.

Finding the divisor

As the divisor grows, every upward quota falls, so the total falls too. That makes it easy to hunt for a divisor whose total is exactly the number of seats: keep halving the search interval around the crossing. The logic test does this on thousands of random countries and checks the two quota columns against the applet's own floor and ceiling operations.

What the check found

The method has a genuine flaw. Several states can lose a seat at the very same divisor, making the upward total jump over the seat count — for about one country in a hundred tried by the logic test, no divisor gives an exact total, and the page says "no divisor fits". Adams' method was never adopted by the US Congress. When a divisor is found, though, the test confirms that its upward quotas always add to exactly the number of seats, and that the lower and upward quotas bracket the standard one.

Set three states and twenty-three seats. Can you make the upward total land on 23 by hand before pressing Find divisor?
